  – Tylenol Children's / Infants', syrup 160 mg/5 ml: 4.6 ml
  – syrup 120 mg/5 ml: 6.2 ml
  – syrup 125 mg/5 ml: 6 ml

q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text:
Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to a child over 6 months old for fever, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Give it every 6 to 8 hours, and check the packaging or leaflet to make sure it suits your child [3][6]. Know your child's weight before giving it [6].

Do not give ibuprofen if your child is dehydrated, has chickenpox, or has asthma unless a doctor recommends it [2]. Do not alternate ibuprofen and paracetamol unless a doctor or nurse tells you to [2].

Keep breastfeeding or offering plenty of fluids, and watch for signs of dehydration [3].

Get medical advice if:
- You are worried about your child [3]
- The medicine is not helping [3]
- A rash appears with the high temperature [2]
- The temperature lasts 5 days or more [2]
- They are not feeding or not themselves [2]

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
Vomiting twice in a morning is often gastroenteritis, which is usually not serious in healthy people but can lead to dehydration, according to MedlinePlus [2]. The main thing is to keep fluids going in.

Wait 20 minutes after a vomit, then give oral rehydration solution — 2 to 5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, says the SEUP [3]. Watch how well he takes it; if he keeps it down, you can slowly give it more often [3]. Don't use homemade solutions like lemonade or commercial soft drinks [3]. Oral rehydration solutions for children can be bought without a prescription [5].

Get help if:
- He is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds [7]
- He vomits a lot, can't keep down solids or liquids, or vomits even without drinking [7]
- The vomit is green, bloody, or looks like coffee grounds [7]
- He is drowsy, limp, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, or urinates little [7]
- Severe belly pain or headache [7]

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, and vomiting is one of the causes, according to MedlinePlus [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, so the priority is to keep fluids going in, says the SEUP [3][5].

When your child vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give oral rehydration solution — 2 to 5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour [5]. Watch how well they take it; if they keep it down, you can slowly give it more often [5]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks [5]. Oral rehydration fluids from the pharmacy are the most helpful for mild dehydration, and sports drinks without caffeine can help a little, according to the CDC [2][4].

Get help if:
- They are listless or very drowsy [3]
- They vomit many times or refuse all fluids [3]
- Vomit is green, bloody, or looks like coffee grounds [6]
- You think they are severely dehydrated [2]

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that keeps a child awake at night is common with colds and other respiratory infections, and in preschool children viral infections are the main cause of wheezing, according to the SEUP [2].

There is no home remedy in these passages for settling a night cough. What the sources describe is what to watch for: a cough that comes in fits, vomiting during or after the fits, and exhaustion afterwards points to whooping cough, according to MedlinePlus [1]. In whooping cough the fits get worse and more frequent, especially at night, and can last up to 10 weeks or more [1].

Get help if:
- The cough comes in fits of many rapid coughs, or ends in a whoop [1]
- They vomit during or after coughing fits [1]
- They are exhausted after coughing fits [1]
- The chest sucks in, the ribs and collarbones show, or they breathe faster than normal [5]
- The lips look blue [5]

Asthma is diagnosed by a doctor, not from a cough alone, and in small children it can be hard to tell apart from repeated respiratory infections, according to MedlinePlus [3].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. One thing to know: whooping cough also starts like a cold, with a runny nose and mild, occasional cough that may last 1 to 2 weeks before the coughing fits begin [1].

What to do now: keep offering fluids and let your son rest. There is no medicine in these sources that shortens a cough after a cold.

Get medical care if:
- Coughing fits that come in bursts, worse at night [1]
- A high-pitched "whoop" sound between coughs [1]
- Vomiting during or after coughing fits [1]
- Exhaustion after coughing fits [1]
- In a baby: pauses in breathing or turning blue — get care right away [1]

If he is breathing fast, his ribs are pulling in, or he is struggling to feed, that needs checking too [5].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without a fever, with normal eating, is usually nothing to worry about. A high temperature is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, according to the NHS [1].

Keep offering fluids and let him rest. If he does develop a fever, the AEPap advises checking his temperature with a digital thermometer, taking it in the armpit, and starting with physical measures: removing extra clothing, giving liquids, reducing physical activity, and a lukewarm bath if he is comfortable [5]. Paracetamol or ibuprofen can relieve the discomfort that comes with fever, with paracetamol the first choice, according to the PUC Chile [4].

Get help if he:
- has a fever and is under 3 months old [1]
- has a fever with a rash [1]
- has a fever lasting 5 days or more [1]
- does not want to eat or is not his usual self [1]
- is dehydrated — fewer wet nappies, sunken eyes, no tears [1]

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
Red spots on the skin can have several causes, and the NHS describes rashes in babies and children [4]. Chickenpox spots can appear anywhere on the body and may be red, pink, darker or the same colour as the surrounding skin, depending on skin tone [4].

If it is chickenpox, the NHS says you can treat it at home: give plenty of fluids, give paracetamol for pain and discomfort, cut your child's fingernails and put socks on their hands at night to stop scratching, use cooling creams or gels, and bathe in cool water and pat the skin dry [1]. Do not give ibuprofen unless a doctor tells you to, as it may cause serious skin infections, and do not give aspirin to children under 16 [1].

Get help if:
- swelling around the mouth or struggling to breathe [5]
- the spots become infected or your child seems very unwell [1]

q: my 2 year old has little red bumps on his legs and keeps scratching them
text:
It is common for a child with hives to have raised, itchy bumps that come in different shapes and sizes, according to the NHS [1]. Hives can be very itchy, and scratching can make the skin redder and more swollen [4].

A pharmacist can advise on antihistamine treatment for a hives rash, though this may not be suitable for young children [7]. Keep your child's nails short and their skin cool to reduce scratching.

Get help immediately if:
- Lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swell [7]
- Breathing is very fast or struggling [7]
- Throat feels tight or struggling to swallow [7]
- Skin, tongue or lips turn blue, grey or pale [7]
- Child becomes very confused, drowsy or dizzy, or is limp or not responding [7]

These can be signs of a serious allergic reaction needing hospital treatment [7].

q: these spots dont seem to bother her but there are more every morning
text:
Spots that do not bother your child are often a rash that can be treated at home, and nappy rash is common in babies [2]. Nappy rash can show as red or raw patches, or as spots, pimples or blisters on the bottom or nappy area, and the skin may be scaly and dry [2]. Keep the area clean and dry, change nappies often, and use a barrier cream at each change; if the rash is not settling, a pharmacist can advise on treatment [2].

Get help if:
- Your child seems uncomfortable or distressed [2]
- The skin becomes itchy or painful [2]
- The spots spread or change [2]
- Your child develops a fever or seems unwell [2]

If the spots are not in the nappy area, or your child has other symptoms, see your doctor.
sources: [2] NHS — "Nappy rash" (2026), section "Nappy rash", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/baby/caring

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, and most children recover quickly [3][6]. Your son may have a headache, feel dizzy, be sick, or be sleepy — these are common after a knock [1].

What you can do: let him rest, physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours depending on how hard the knock was — no sport and no screens during that time, then a gradual return to normal activity [4]. He can eat and drink as usual, according to his appetite [6]. If he has a headache, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen at the dose your doctor indicates [6]. He may sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6].

Get help if:
- Intense or worsening headache, or one that does not improve with the usual medicine [4]
- Repeated vomiting [4]
- Confusion, or hard to wake [4]
- Changes in behaviour, trouble speaking or walking [4]
- Blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [4]

Watch him over the first 24 hours after the knock for signs of seriousness [3].

q: he fell off the couch and vomited once about an hour later
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomiting after a head injury
text:
Vomiting once about an hour after a fall is one of the usual symptoms of a head knock, according to the SEUP [7]. A fall from higher than a metre, or a child under three months, are reasons the same guidance says to be checked [1].

While you are on the way, keep them lying on their side so that if they vomit again it does not go into their airway, and do not give them anything to eat or drink [3]. Do not leave them alone, and check that they wake and respond normally [7].

The signs that make a head injury more serious, per the SEUP, are: being drowsy or floppy, confusion or memory loss, a headache that gets worse, vomiting that keeps going, or any behaviour that worries you [1][3][7].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text:
At around 6 months, your baby is ready to start solid foods, and at first how much they eat matters less than getting used to the idea of eating [2]. They will still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [2].

Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows, and introduce one food at a time so you can spot any allergic reaction, such as a rash, diarrhoea or vomiting [1][3]. Offer a variety of foods, following your family's usual foods, and build up to 2–3 meals a day between 6 and 8 months [2][3][6].

Foods to avoid for now:
- No honey before 12 months — risk of botulism [1]
- No cow's milk before 12 months [1]
- No unpasteurised drinks or foods [1]
- No juice before 12 months [1]
- Avoid choking foods like whole nuts, popcorn and whole grapes [1]

If your baby was born prematurely, ask your health visitor or doctor when to start [2].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text: For a 9-month-old, breast milk or formula stays the main drink, and the extra fluids come with meals and during illness, according to the WHO [1]. Offer water in small amounts with meals rather than large volumes, and keep breastfeeding on demand — the AEP says breast milk remains the main food between 6 and 12 months and should be given on demand without reducing feeds [2]. During illness, increase fluid intake, including how often you breastfeed, and offer soft, favourite foods [1]. If your baby is not breastfed, the AEP recommends follow-on formula after 6 months [2]. There is no fixed amount of water a 9-month-old should drink in these passages; let thirst and feeds guide you, and ask your doctor if you are worried about how much they are drinking.

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text: It is common for babies to prefer fruit, and the way to build vegetable acceptance is repeated, varied offering rather than pressure. Introduce the whole range of fruits and vegetables gradually, at any daily meal, and vary how you present them — puréed, mashed or in small pieces [2]. The taste for different flavours, including bitter ones like some vegetables, is formed early, and early exposure to different flavours may reduce the risk of refusing new foods [2]. Offer vegetables alongside fruit at meals, and keep offering even when they are refused. Fruit juice offers no nutritional benefit over whole fruit and can displace other foods, so give whole fruit instead [2]. Continue milk feeds alongside meals, and include iron-containing foods such as dark green vegetables, beans and lentils [1].

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text:
At 13 months, formula is no longer needed — your child can drink pasteurised whole cows' milk as their main drink, according to the NHS [6]. They should be eating 3 meals a day with a variety of foods, plus 2 healthy snacks between meals [6].

Offer starchy foods like potatoes, bread and rice; fruit and vegetables; full-fat dairy such as cheese and yoghurt; and protein from meat, fish, eggs, beans or lentils [6]. Give full-fat dairy products, as children under 2 need the vitamins and extra energy in them [6]. Unsweetened, calcium-fortified milk alternatives like soya, oat or almond drinks can be their main drink from age 1 [6].

Ask your health visitor or doctor for advice if you are finding the move away from formula difficult [3].

q: how often should a newborn poop
text:
It is normal for a newborn's pooping to vary a lot: the rhythm and consistency of stools differ from one baby to another, and it is not essential that a baby poops every day, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more is whether the stools are soft and the baby is comfortable, since constipation means stools that are too hard, with pain or incomplete emptying [6].

For a baby under 6 months, keep feeding as usual with breast milk or formula [3]. Do not give laxatives or enemas without asking your doctor [3].

In a baby this young, check with your doctor if there is:

- Blood in the stool [3]
- Bad belly pain, or the baby is very floppy and crying a lot [3]
- Vomiting many times, not keeping down food or fluids [3]

Your doctor can also advise on what is normal for your baby's feeding.

q: my 9 month old suddenly wakes up every two hours at night
text:
It is common and normal for a 9-month-old to wake at night: night wakings are a natural phenomenon at least during the first year of life, according to the Junta de Andalucía [4]. A breastfed baby may need to feed between 1 and 5 times a night [4].

What you can do: keep night feeds calm and dim, and settle your baby back to sleep after each waking — if your baby sleeps in your bed you may rest better and not notice some of the feeds, since the baby falls asleep again afterwards [4]. Only you can decide how long your baby sleeps in your room or bed [4].

Do not sleep with your baby on a sofa, and do not leave your baby alone to sleep in an adult bed, a waterbed or a mattress that sinks [4].

If you are extremely tired, or if you or your partner smoke, have drunk alcohol, or have taken drugs or medicines that make you sleep more heavily than usual, bed-sharing is not safe [4].

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on at night or early in the morning is one of the symptoms of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Asthma can be hard to diagnose in small children, because it looks like other childhood conditions and some children have symptoms only now and then, so it can seem like they are having one respiratory infection after another [6].

If you think your child may have asthma, the doctor can examine him, ask about his history, and may try asthma medicines for several weeks to see whether the symptoms get better [6].

Get medical help right away if your child has severe coughing, serious trouble breathing, or turns very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [3].

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text:
Using albuterol more often than usual can be a sign the asthma is not fully controlled, and the SEUP says most flare-ups are mild and can be treated at home with bronchodilators [3]. Give salbutamol with a spacer device (and a mask for small children), never straight into the mouth, because it works less well that way [3][7]. A spacer is a plastic container with a mouthpiece or mask at one end and a hole for the inhaler at the other, and a homemade one from a 500 ml plastic bottle can work as well as a bought one [2]. If there is no clear improvement, go to a health centre [7].

Get help urgently if:
- Very agitated or drowsy, or turning blue or pale [7]
- Breathing getting faster, ribs showing, belly or chest pulling in [7]
- Needing inhalations every two hours or less [7]

Avoid smoke and, during the flare-up, exercise and allergens [3].

q: my daughter is breathing faster after running but gets better when she rests

- The chest hurts when they breathe [4]

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be a sign of croup, which is an inflammation of the voice box and windpipe, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It often starts like a cold and then causes hoarseness, a barking cough and high-pitched sounds when breathing [3]. Most viral cases are mild and can be treated at home, and symptoms usually get worse at night and last three to five days [3].

Keep her calm and comfortable, and offer fluids often. Croup is more common in children between six months and three years, and in autumn and winter [3].

Get help if:
- Breathing becomes difficult or she seems to be struggling [3]
- She is drowsy, floppy or very irritable [1][4]
- Her ribs pull in or her chest sinks with each breath [1][4]
- She is breathing fast or tiring when walking or running [1]
- Her colour looks wrong [4]

If you are worried about her breathing, call your doctor straight away [3].

q: my 6 year old says his chest hurts when he takes a deep breath
text:
Chest pain when breathing deeply can have several causes, and one of them is asthma: chest tightness that makes it hard to breathe deeply is a common symptom, according to the WHO [1]. Symptoms like this are often worse at night or during exercise, and can also be triggered by a cold, dust, smoke, pollen or strong smells [1]. Because symptoms like these can be caused by other conditions too, the WHO advises talking to a healthcare provider [1].

The SEUP says to watch at home for difficulty breathing — ribs showing or the chest sinking in, fast breathing, or getting tired when walking or running — and for chest pain when breathing [2]. Go to the emergency department if your child's general condition worsens, if they are listless, sleepy or very irritable, or if breathing becomes difficult [2]. Chest pain on breathing is also listed by the SEUP as a reason to be seen urgently, to rule out complications [5].

q: my daughter is crying nonstop after a fall and wont calm down
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: A fall down stairs or from more than a metre, or crying that will not settle after a knock: get a doctor to see them today
text:
A knock on the head can cause headache, confusion, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1]. Crying that will not settle after a knock is a reason for a doctor to see her today, and the SEUP says a fall from more than a metre or a child under three months should also be checked in the emergency department [4].

While you get her seen, keep her calm and do not leave her alone. The SEUP advises watching a child closely in the first 24 hours after a knock for signs of seriousness [2].

Signs that mean it is more serious, according to the SEUP [6]:
- Intense or worsening headache that does not improve with the usual medicine
- Repeated vomiting
- Disorientation or confusion; in very small children, being irritable or hard to wake
- Changes in usual behaviour, trouble speaking or walking
- Blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears

q: can babies get dehydrated from breastfeeding
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
Breastfeeding is not a cause of dehydration — breast milk is a fluid, and the WHO lists exclusive breastfeeding in the first six months as one of the key measures for preventing diarrhoeal disease [5]. Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, from diarrhoea, vomiting, sweating, fever or simply not drinking enough [1].

If your baby is having diarrhoea or vomiting, keep breastfeeding normally, and even more often if they want it, according to the SEUP [3]. Offer smaller amounts more frequently to reduce the risk of vomiting [3]. Oral rehydration solution is what replaces the water and salts lost, and it is absorbed in the small intestine [5]; sports drinks should be avoided in children with diarrhoea because they contain too much sugar and the wrong electrolytes [3].

Get help if:
- Vomiting a lot, or unable to keep down solids or liquids [3]
- Green vomit, blood, or brown coffee-ground material [3]
- Blood in the stool, or diarrhoea that keeps going [5]
- Signs of dehydration [5]

q: should I give my daughter the HPV vaccine
text:
The HPV vaccine protects against human papillomavirus, a common virus spread through skin contact, usually during sex. Some types are linked to cancers including cervical, mouth, anal, penile, vulval and vaginal cancer, and genital warts, according to the NHS [1]. It works very well: since it has been used there has been a big drop in conditions linked to HPV, such as cervical cancer and genital warts [2].

The NHS recommends it for children aged 12 to 13, though in the United States the ages follow the national schedule, so ask your doctor when your daughter is due [1].

The most common side effects are mild and do not last long: swelling or pain where the injection was given, headache, a high temperature, dizziness, feeling sick, tiredness [5]. A severe allergic reaction is very rare, and the person who vaccinates is trained to treat it immediately [5].

If she has been vaccinated, she should still attend cervical screening when she is older, as there is still a small chance of cervical cancer [2].

q: my 11 year old needs a tetanus shot after a cut, does he need one
text:
Tetanus enters the body through cuts or wounds, and it is preventable with vaccines that contain tetanus toxoid, according to the WHO [4]. An 11-year-old is past the age for DTaP, which is only for children younger than 7; different vaccines against tetanus, diphtheria and pertussis (Tdap and Td) are used for older children and adolescents, according to MedlinePlus [1].

Whether he needs a shot now depends on his vaccination history and the wound, which only his doctor can assess. Tell the provider if he has had an allergic reaction after a previous dose of any tetanus, diphtheria or pertussis vaccine, or any severe, life-threatening allergies [1]. Children with minor illnesses, such as a cold, may still be vaccinated [3].

Get medical help if you see:
- A wound that is deep, dirty or won't stop bleeding
- Muscle stiffness or spasms, especially of the jaw or neck [5]
- Trouble swallowing or breathing [5]
- Fever with sweating [5]

The vaccination ages follow the United States national schedule.

q: can I give Tylenol after vaccines

Yes, you can give a medication to help with pain or to lower a fever after vaccination if needed, according to the Government of Canada [1]. Mild side effects are normal — fussiness, a mild fever, sleepiness, or pain, swelling or redness where the shot was given — and they go away on their own within hours to a few days [1].

Check with your child's health care provider if you need advice about which medication to use [1].

Get help right away if your child has signs of a serious allergic reaction: breathing problems (wheezing), swelling of the face, tongue or throat, or a red rash on the skin (hives) [1]. Also contact your health care provider if other symptoms are getting worse or not going away, or if you're worried for any other reason [1].

q: I gave my son Tylenol and he vomited 10 minutes later
text:
Vomiting after a dose of paracetamol (Tylenol) is common and usually not a reason to worry, according to the NHS [5]. Do not give another dose straight away — wait and check the leaflet before giving it to your child [5]. The most important thing is to keep fluids going: offer small sips of water often, and if he is on formula or solid foods, give small sips of water between feeds [5]. Let him rest [5].

Get help if:
- He vomits a lot, cannot keep down solids or liquids, or vomits even when he has taken nothing [2]
- The vomit is green, contains blood, or looks like coffee grounds [2]
- He is drowsy, limp, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, or passes little urine [2]
- He has severe tummy pain or a headache [2]

text:
Heavy periods are common in the first years after a girl's first period, and about half of all teenage girls have irregular periods in the first year, according to the Ecimed guidelines [2]. - More than 6 well-soaked pads a day [6]
- Clots in the blood [6]

- Cycles shorter than 21 days [6]
- Bleeding between periods [3]

q: my child has asthma but is not wheezing right now, should I still use albuterol
text:
No, if there is no wheezing or trouble breathing right now, the sources describe salbutamol as the treatment for an asthma attack — the episodes of cough, breathlessness and chest wheezing caused by narrowed airways — and not as something to give when the child is well [1][4]. The SEUP says that in any child having bronchospasm you start treatment with salbutamol, and that inhalers must always be given with a spacer, never straight into the mouth [7].

If an attack does start, give 2 to 4 puffs of salbutamol one at a time through a spacer, with a face mask for small children, and repeat that dose after 10 to 15 minutes [6]. Keep the child resting, away from tobacco smoke and pollution, and continue any maintenance treatment during the attack [6].

Get help if:
- Very agitated or drowsy, or turning blue or pale [7]
- Breathing gets faster, ribs pull in, belly moves a lot [7]
- Puffs needed every two hours or less [7]
- No clear improvement after treatment at home [6]

q: I found a lump behind my baby's ear, should I worry
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Swelling or redness behind the ear, or the ear pushed forward: it should be seen today
text:
A lump behind the ear in a baby is often a swollen lymph node, which can happen with ear infections or other infections, and ear infections are very common in children [2][6]. Most ear infections clear up on their own within 3 days, though symptoms can sometimes last up to a week [2].

While you wait to be seen, treat any pain: give paracetamol or ibuprofen every 6 to 8 hours for the first 1 to 2 days, before the pain builds up [3]. Do not put anything in the ear to ease the pain, and keep the ear dry, especially if it has been discharging [3]. If your baby is feeding, frequent saline nose washes can help [3]. It is normal for them to have a small appetite, so do not force them to eat [3].

Watch for signs it is getting worse: redness, pain or swelling behind the ear, or the ear pushed forward [5]; a lot of drowsiness or being very irritable [5]; or no improvement after 48 to 72 hours of pain relief [5].

q: my toddler has a swollen eyelid after waking up
text:
A swollen eyelid on waking can be part of a common viral illness in toddlers. Roseola, which mainly affects babies and toddlers, can cause swollen eyelids along with a sudden high temperature, cold-like symptoms such as a sore throat, runny nose and cough, and loss of appetite, according to the NHS [3]. These symptoms usually last 3 to 5 days, and then a rash of pinkish-red spots appears, starting on the chest, tummy and back before spreading to the face, neck and arms; it normally fades within 2 days [3].

Swollen eyelids can also be a sign of an allergic reaction. In a severe allergic reaction, swelling of the eyelids can appear along with itching, hives, widespread redness, trouble breathing, sneezing, dizziness, loss of consciousness or vomiting, according to the SEUP [6].

Get help if:
- Trouble breathing or noisy breathing [5]
- Drooling or blue lips [5]
- Pale skin [5]
- Loss of consciousness [5]

q: my child has a fever but his hands are freezing cold
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Cold hands and feet in a child with fever: it may be poor circulation, get it checked
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, cold hands and feet with a fever happen because the body is raising its temperature: the blood vessels in the skin narrow to keep heat in, which can cause chills and cold extremities, according to the SEUP [7].

What to do now: check the temperature with a thermometer, under the arm is fine [5]. If there are no warning signs, start with physical measures — take off extra clothing, offer fluids, reduce activity, and a lukewarm bath only if the child is comfortable [5]. Do not undress or sponge the child to cool them, and do not wrap them in too many clothes or blankets [2]. If the child is uncomfortable, you can give the usual antipyretic your paediatrician recommends; the dose depends on age and weight [6].

Get help if:
- Drowsy, not reacting, or very irritable [1]
- Difficulty breathing [1]
- Spots that do not fade when pressed [1]
- Not keeping down solids or liquids [1]
- Skin colour blue, grey, pale or blotchy, or lips/tongue pale or blue [2]

Confusion after a knock to the head is one of the symptoms the SEUP lists for a head injury, along with headache, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness [1].

While you get help, keep him with you and do not leave him alone. Let him rest, without physical activity, sport or screens [5]. Do not give him anything to eat or drink in case he needs to be seen.

q: she hit her head last week and has been completely normal until today
text:
Most head injuries are not serious, but it's important to get medical help for any symptoms, according to the NHS [3]. A head injury can cause concussion, a temporary brain injury that can last a few weeks [3].

Get urgent medical help if she has been knocked out and has not woken up, cannot stay awake, has a fit, has problems with vision or hearing, has clear fluid coming from her ears or nose, has new numbness or weakness, or has problems walking, balancing, understanding or speaking [3]. For the headache, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen in the dose your doctor indicates [5]. She can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking her every 4 hours [5]. Rest from sport and screens for 24 to 48 hours, then return to normal activities gradually [2].

banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:

What to do now: hold her upright against your shoulder and comfort her, and let her calm down. If she has a cold, keep her nose clear and offer fluids often. - Feeding much less than normal, or a dry nappy for 12 hours or more [2]
- She seems to be getting worse [2]

- Breathing becomes difficult after a coughing bout [4]

q: my baby has red cheeks but no fever
text:

A single weight on its own cannot tell whether a child is growing well: what matters is the weight for the child's height and how it changes over time on their growth curve, according to the PUC Chile manual [4]. Growth is judged against the WHO 2006 standards, and the position on the curve is expressed as a z-score — the number of standard deviations above or below the average [4]. q: my 18 month old has a fever of 103 and won't take Tylenol
text:
103 °F = 39.4 °C.

A fever is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most children get better on their own [1]. The main goal is keeping your child comfortable and well hydrated, not bringing the number down by itself [3].

If your child won't take Tylenol, you can try acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) — both reduce fever in children [4]. Acetaminophen can be given every 4 to 6 hours, ibuprofen every 6 to 8 hours, and ibuprofen should not be used in children under 6 months [4]. The dose depends on your child's weight, so check the label or ask your doctor [4]. Offer plenty of fluids, keep the room comfortably cool, and don't bundle them up [3]. Don't force food if they don't want it [3].

Get help if your child:

- is very drowsy or hard to wake
- has trouble breathing
- has a rash that doesn't fade when pressed

What helps now: offer plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration [1]. If your child is uncomfortable, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen — paracetamol is the usual first choice [4]. You can also remove extra clothing, offer fluids and give a lukewarm bath if your child is comfortable [5].

- Your child is very sleepy, confused, irritable or behaving oddly [6]
- Severe headache or repeated vomiting [6]
- A seizure (convulsion) [6]
- Fever above 41 °C (105.8 °F), or any fever in a child who looks very unwell [4][5]

q: he has an inhaler but I dont know when to use it
text:
When the chest tightens and breathing gets hard, the inhaler is the treatment: the airways open up with bronchodilators like salbutamol, according to the SEUP [2]. Give it through a spacer, never straight into the mouth — it works better that way, and for a small child add a mask [4]. Most flare-ups are mild and can be handled at home with the inhaler; symptoms usually settle in a few days, though they can last up to a week [4].

Get help if:
- He is very restless or sleepy, or turns blue or pale [1]
- Breathing gets worse: faster, ribs showing, chest pulling in [1]
- He needs the inhaler every two hours or more often [1]

q: my child has chickenpox, when can he go back to school
text:
Chickenpox is very contagious, and children usually miss 5 to 6 days of school or childcare because of it, according to the CDC [1]. A person with chickenpox can pass it on until all the spots have crusted over [2].

Keep him at home while he is still infectious. The contagious period runs from 1 to 2 days before the rash appears until about 5 to 6 days after it starts, and until all the blisters have turned into crusts [2]. So he can go back to school once every spot has crusted over [2].

For the itch, calamine creams and lotions and oatmeal baths can help, and acetaminophen can help with fever — do not give aspirin, because with chickenpox it can cause Reye syndrome [3].

Get medical help if:
- The rash or fever seems severe, or he seems very unwell [3]
- He has a weakened immune system, or is a baby or teenager — these cases can be more serious [3]

q: my 10 month old is pulling his ear and crying a lot
text:
Ear infections are a common cause of ear pulling and crying in babies, and most clear up on their own within 3 days, according to the NHS [3]. Other signs to look for are fluid draining from the ear, trouble sleeping, and being irritable or off their food [3][1].

For the pain, MedlinePlus says your health care provider may recommend pain relievers [1]. The SEUP advises treating the pain regularly with ibuprofen or paracetamol every 6-8 hours for the first 1-2 days, before the pain builds up [6]. Do not put anything in the ear to soothe it, and keep the ear dry, especially if it has been discharging [6]. If your baby is feeding, frequent saline nose washes help [6]. If an antibiotic has been prescribed, follow the dose, interval and duration exactly [6].

See your doctor if:
- Pain is severe or your baby is very distressed [1]
- High temperature [3]
- Discharge from the ear [3]
- Symptoms last more than a week [3]
- Your baby is not feeding or is hard to wake [3]

q: my 3 year old keeps vomiting every time he drinks water
text:
Small sips of water or sucking on ice chips can help when a child is having trouble keeping liquids down, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Offer fluids in small amounts more often than usual, and give regular small sips of rehydration solution to replace lost fluids — your pharmacist can recommend one [3]. Do not give fruit juice or fizzy drinks, as these can make vomiting worse [3][5].

Get help if:
- Vomiting a lot, not keeping down solids or liquids, or vomiting even without drinking [2]
- Vomit that is green, contains blood, or looks like coffee grounds [2]
- Drowsy, limp, very thirsty, sunken eyes, crying without tears, or passing little urine [2]
- Severe belly pain or headache [2]

q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text:
Hard, painful poops are constipation: the stool is hard and dry and it can hurt to pass [3]. It is common and in most cases it lasts a short time and is not serious [3].

What helps, according to the SEUP: offer more liquids, preferably water, to soften the stool and make it easier to pass; add more fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables; and do not replace fruit with juice, because juice has little fibre [1]. Keep to a regular routine and don't let him hold in the urge to go [1]. Laxatives or enemas should not be given without asking your paediatrician [1].

See your doctor if:
- Bad abdominal pain, or he is very down and complaining a lot [1]
- Blood in the stool [1]
- Vomiting many times, unable to keep down solids or liquids [1]
- Pain when passing stool, or anal fissures [2][4]

Most cases of constipation in children are not caused by any illness [1].

q: my baby is sleeping more today but wakes up and drinks normally
text:
It is common for babies to have their own pattern of waking and sleeping, and this is unlikely to be the same as other babies you know, according to the NHS [1]. All babies change their sleep patterns, and growth spurts, teething and illnesses can all affect how your baby sleeps [2].

If your baby is having problems sleeping or you need more advice about getting into a routine, speak to your health visitor [2].

To keep sleep safe: always put your baby to sleep on their back on a firm, flat mattress, and keep pillows, sheets and blankets away from them [3]. Do not swaddle them — baby sleeping bags are safer [3]. Keep the room at about 16 to 20C, and check their temperature by feeling their chest or the back of their neck; cool hands and feet are normal [6]. Remove layers if their skin is hot or sweating, and take off hats and extra clothing as soon as you come indoors or get into a car, bus or train, even if it means waking your baby [6].

q: my baby has been vomiting for six hours but still wants to breastfeed
text:
A vomiting illness in a baby usually settles on its own within less than a week, according to the SEUP [4]. Keep breastfeeding — offer the breast normally, and even more often if your baby wants it [3]. Small amounts more often are easier to keep down than a full feed [2].

If your baby is on formula or solids, give small sips of extra water (boiled and cooled first if under 6 months) [2]. Ask your pharmacist about an oral rehydration solution for the small sips that replace lost fluids [2]. Do not give fruit juice or fizzy drinks — they can make vomiting worse [2].

- Vomit that is green, bloody, or looks like coffee grounds [5]
- Sleepy, floppy, very thirsty, sunken eyes, crying without tears, or passing little urine [5]
- Severe tummy pain or headache [5]

q: what temperature counts as a fever in a newborn
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Baby under 3 months with fever (≥38 °C / 100.4 °F)
text:
A fever in a newborn is a temperature of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher, according to the NHS [3]. A normal temperature varies a little from child to child, and a high temperature is 38 °C (100.4 °F) or more [3].

For a baby this young, do not give any medicine at home. Keep breastfeeding or offering fluids as normal, and check on them regularly, including during the night [4]. Take their temperature with a digital thermometer placed in the top of the armpit, holding the arm gently against their side, and leave it in as long as the leaflet says [3].

Get help today — babies under 3 months with a temperature of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher need to be seen [2].

q: my son passed out after standing in the sun for a long time
banner: 🚨 Call 911 now or go to the emergency department. | Reason: Not responding to stimuli
text:
Fainting can happen when not enough blood or oxygen reaches the brain, and standing a long time in extreme heat is one of the situations that can bring it on, according to the SEUP [2]. While you get help, move him to a cool, shaded place, take off extra clothing, apply cool wet cloths to his forehead, neck and armpits, and offer sips of cool water [7]. Use a fan to help lower his body temperature [7].

Heat stroke is serious and can affect children, especially in high temperatures [6]. Signs that make it more serious include hot, red, dry skin, a high fever over 39°C (102.2 °F), confusion or disorientation, a severe headache, nausea or vomiting, and loss of consciousness [6].

q: my 2 year old fell off the sofa and was sick once
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomiting after a head injury
text:
A head injury is the medical term for a blow to the head, which usually happens from a fall, and the usual symptoms include headache, confusion, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1]. Keep your child resting, both physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours depending on how hard the blow was, with no sport and no screens, and return to normal activities gradually [5].

While you get help, watch for signs that mean it is more serious: repeated vomiting, intense or worsening headache, confusion or disorientation, being very irritable or hard to wake, or blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [5]. In a child this age, vomiting or nausea that keeps coming back, trouble speaking, weakness in the arms or legs, or growing confusion are also warning signs, according to MedlinePlus [4].

q: my child keeps scratching red patches on his arms
text:
Itchy red patches on the arms are common in children, and eczema is one of the usual causes: it makes skin dry and itchy, and scratching reddens it and makes the itch worse [2]. Eczema is not contagious [2].

What helps is a good skin-care routine and avoiding the things that irritate the skin, such as certain soaps, fabrics and lotions, stress, and things the child is allergic to like certain foods, pollen and animals [2]. Treatments can include medicines, skin creams and light therapy [2].

See your doctor if the patches do not get better in about a month [1], or if the skin becomes sore, crusted or filled with pus, which can mean a bacterial infection such as impetigo [6].

q: my toddler is wheezing after running around outside
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
Wheezing after running is a common pattern: bronchial obstruction that gets worse with exercise, and in preschool children the main cause of wheezing is viral respiratory infections, according to the SEUP [2]. Asthma causes wheezing, cough and chest tightness when the airways narrow [3].

What to do now: keep your child calm and sitting upright, and let them rest — symptoms often start after physical effort [7]. If your child has been prescribed a bronchodilator such as salbutamol, this is the medicine that relieves the obstruction; give it as your doctor or the leaflet instructs [2].

Get help now if:
- Severe trouble breathing, intense cough, or difficulty speaking [7]
- Chest, ribs or collarbones pulling in, or breathing faster than normal [7]
- Bluish colour around the lips [7]
- Paleness or bluish colour in the face, lips or nails [4]

A severe attack can come on gradually or suddenly and can be life-threatening [4].

q: my 4 year old has earache after a cold
text:
An earache after a cold is often acute otitis media — infection and inflammation of the middle ear, behind the eardrum. It usually happens as a complication of an upper respiratory cold with a lot of nasal mucus, according to the SEUP [5].

For the pain, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen; the dose depends on your child's weight, and PediBot's dose calculator can work it out for you.

Get help if:
- Your child becomes very drowsy, floppy or very irritable [4]
- Breathing becomes difficult — ribs showing, chest pulling in, fast breathing [4]
- The earache is severe or does not improve

Most children with earache after a cold get better, but if the pain is bad or lasts more than a day or two, see your doctor.

A blocked nose is common with a cold, and cold symptoms usually last 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [3]. To help your baby feed and breathe more easily, the NHS suggests saline nose drops from a pharmacy for a blocked nose, and smaller feeds more often [1]. The SEUP adds nose washes to keep the nose clear of mucus, small frequent feeds to keep feeding and hydration good, and a semi-upright position to make breathing easier [2]. - Your baby is floppy and will not wake or stay awake [7]

q: my 2 year old has a temperature of 39.2 and cold hands
text:
A temperature of 39.2°C with cold hands is a fever, and in a 2-year-old the usual cause is a viral infection of the nose and throat, which is very common in the first years of life, according to the SEUP [6]. Fever, when it appears, usually settles within 2 or 3 days [4].

What to do now: offer plenty of fluids, and if the fever is above 38°C and your child is uncomfortable, give the usual anti-fever medicine your paediatrician recommends [4]. Keep your child away from smoke [4]. Do not use cough or cold medicines, especially under 6 years old [4].

Get help if:
- Your child is floppy, drowsy or very irritable [5]
- Breathing becomes difficult — ribs pulling in, fast breathing [5]
- Feeding or drinking much less than normal [2]
- A dry nappy for 12 hours or more [2]
- You are worried about your child [2]

q: can I give Nurofen as well
text: Yes, you can give ibuprofen for children instead if paracetamol is not helping their symptoms, according to the NHS [2]. Do not give ibuprofen and paracetamol at the same time, but you can alternate between them if a doctor or nurse tells you to [2]. If you do this, write down when you gave each medicine so the doses are spaced evenly and you avoid giving too much [2]. Ibuprofen can be given 3 to 4 times in 24 hours, depending on your child's age and dose — check the packet or leaflet [2]. The dose goes by weight, not age [5]. Ibuprofen should not be given if your child is vomiting continuously, or is under 3 months or under 5 kg [5].

q: my 5 year old complains of stomach ache and won't eat anything
text:
Stomach ache and refusing food can happen with a tummy bug: norovirus causes vomiting and diarrhoea, and you may also have a headache, tummy pain and body aches, according to the NHS [4]. It usually gets better in about 2 days [4].

Offer drinks in small sips often, and let your child rest. If they are not eating much for a day or two, that on its own is not usually a worry — it's more helpful to think about what they eat over a week, and children's tastes change, so keep offering a variety of foods without forcing them [3].

Get help if:
- Stomach pain is severe or getting worse [4]
- They cannot keep any fluids down [4]
- They are drowsy, confused or not themselves [4]

- They have a high temperature that does not settle [4]

text:
Not wetting nappies for 3 hours or more is a sign of dehydration in a baby, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Dehydration happens when a child loses more fluid than they take in, often from diarrhoea, vomiting or fever [3].

Keep offering fluids. If your baby is breastfeeding, keep feeding normally and offer the breast more often if they want it [1]. For mild dehydration, oral rehydration solution for children can be bought without a prescription [4]. If they struggle to keep fluids down, try small sips of water [2].

Get help now if your baby has:

- Crying without tears [6]
- Unusual sleepiness or irritability [6]
- Eyes that look sunken [6]
- Confusion, fainting or fast breathing [6]

q: my baby is 4 months and has a fever of 38
text:
A fever is the body's normal response to fighting an infection, and most children with a high temperature can be looked after at home, according to the NHS [1]. It usually comes down over 1 to 4 days [1].

Keep breastfeeding as normal, and offer plenty of fluids [1]. Check on your baby regularly, including during the night, and keep them at home [1]. Do not undress them or sponge them down to cool them, and do not cover them in too many clothes or bedclothes [7].

Because your baby is 4 months old, a temperature of 38C or higher means you should get medical advice — the NHS advises calling for advice if a child is under 3 months with a temperature of 38C or higher, or 3 to 6 months with 39C or higher [7]. Also get help if:

- they have a rash as well as the fever [7]
- they are not feeding or not their usual self [7]
- they seem dehydrated — fewer wet nappies, sunken eyes, no tears when crying [7]
- the fever lasts 5 days or more [7]

Do not give aspirin to a child under 16 [7]. Paracetamol or ibuprofen can be given if they are distressed, but check the leaflet is suitable for their age, or ask a pharmacist or doctor [1].

q: my child got fever after vaccination yesterday
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, a mild fever in the day or two after a vaccination is a common, expected reaction and usually passes on its own.

Give plenty of fluids and let them rest. Dress them lightly and do not bundle them up. If they are uncomfortable, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen, but the dose depends on your child's age and weight, so ask your doctor or follow the leaflet; PediBot's dose calculator covers these two medicines. - Fever in a baby under 3 months [3]
- Fever that lasts more than a few days or keeps rising
- Your child is drowsy, floppy or hard to wake
- Breathing is fast or difficult

These are general signs; if you are worried, contact your doctor.

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put
text:
Mosquito bites usually just itch, and they get better in a few days, according to the NHS [2]. To calm the itch, a zinc and calamine lotion with menthol, phenol or camphor can be applied, or a short course of a mild topical corticosteroid such as hydrocortisone [5]. - The bites become infected — spreading redness, heat, pus [2]
- She has a serious allergic reaction — swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing [2]
- She seems unwell with fever, or the bites keep spreading [2]

q: मेरे 2 साल के बच्चे को 39 बुखार है, पैरासिटामोल कितनी दूं?
text: बच्चे का वज़न कितना है? पैरासिटामोल की खुराक उम्र से नहीं, वज़न से तय होती है: वज़न बताइए, फिर सही मात्रा बताई जाएगी।

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
text:
दस्त आमतौर पर किसी संक्रमण का लक्षण है और यह कुछ दिनों तक रह सकता है, पर इलाज संभव है [3][5]। WHO के अनुसार दस्त का इलाज मौखिक पुनर्जलीकरण घोल (ORS) से किया जाना चाहिए — यह साफ पानी, नमक और चीनी का घोल है [3]। साथ ही ज़िंक की गोलियाँ दी जाती हैं, जो दस्त की अवधि कम करती हैं और मल की मात्रा घटाती हैं [1][3]। बच्चे को खाना खिलाना बंद न करें: दस्त के दौरान भी पौष्टिक खाना — स्तनपान सहित — जारी रखें, इससे कुपोषण और दस्त का चक्र टूटता है [1]।

मदद कब लें:
- दस्त लंबे समय तक बने रहना (लगातार दस्त) [1]
- मल में खून आना [1]
- निर्जलीकरण के लक्षण दिखना [1]
- गंभीर निर्जलीकरण या शॉक [1]

ORS और ज़िंक की मात्रा और अवधि बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न के अनुसार तय होती है — यह अपने डॉक्टर से पूछें।
sources: [1] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Prevention and treatment", p. 1 — https://www.who
[3] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Overview", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/news-room/f
[5] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Key facts", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/news-room/

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई बीमारियों में हो सकते हैं। खसरे में दाने पहले लक्षणों के 3 से 5 दिन बाद निकलते हैं — आमतौर पर बालों की लाइन पर चेहरे से शुरू होकर गर्दन, धड़, बाज़ुओं, टाँगों और पैरों तक फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है, CDC के अनुसार [4]। चेचक में मुख्य लक्षण खुजली वाला दाना है, जो शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकता है, और दाने से पहले या बाद में तेज़ बुखार, दर्द और भूख न लगना भी हो सकता है, NHS के अनुसार [5]। हाथ-पैर-मुँह रोग में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना, फिर मुँह के छाले और हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे दाने हो सकते हैं [3]।

अगर बच्चे के मुँह के आसपास सूजन हो या साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो, तो तुरंत मदद लें [6]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।
sources: [3] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Symptoms of hand, foot and mout
[4] CDC — "Measles Symptoms and Complications", section "3–5 days after symptoms begin: me
[5] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Symptoms of chickenpox", p. 1 —
[6] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Raised, itchy spots or patches"

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
नमस्ते। 6 महीने के बच्चे का दूध कम पीना और पेशाब कम आना — यह देखने की बात है, और ऊपर बताए संकेतों के साथ आज ही डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

तब तक, जो स्रोत कहते हैं वह करें: स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, और अगर बच्चा माँगे तो उससे भी ज़्यादा बार कराते रहें [1]। बच्चे को भूखा न रखें — थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, बार-बार दूध दें, ताकि उल्टी का जोखिम कम हो [1]।

ध्यान रखें: बच्चे को खेल-खेल में मिलने वाले पेय (स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक) न दें, क्योंकि उनमें चीनी बहुत ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स बच्चे के लिए अनुपयुक्त होते हैं [1]। मीठी चीज़ें और जूस भी न दें [1]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी करे, ठोस या तरल कुछ भी न रुके, या उल्टी हरी, खून वाली या कॉफ़ी जैसी भूरी हो — तो तुरंत डॉक्टर को दिखाएँ [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर तुरंत डॉक्टर से जाँच करानी चाहिए, और SEUP के अनुसार अगर बच्चा तीन महीने से छोटा है या गिरावट एक मीटर से ज़्यादा ऊँचाई से हुई है तो भी आपातकालीन विभाग जाना चाहिए [1]। डॉक्टर ज़रूरी जाँचें करेंगे और देखेंगे कि अतिरिक्त परीक्षण चाहिए या नहीं, हालाँकि ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसकी ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ती [1]।

रास्ते में बच्चे को आराम से लिटाए रखें और होश बनाए रखने के लिए उससे बात करते रहें। अगर बच्चा दूध पीता है तो थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार दूध पिलाते रहें, और उल्टी होने पर छोटे घूँट में पानी दें [5]।

अगर बच्चा बेहोश हो जाए, सुस्त पड़ जाए या ठीक से जवाब न दे, साँस लेने में तकलीफ हो, या उल्टी में खून आए तो तुरंत आपातकालीन मदद लें [3][4]।

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
कब्ज़ से बच्चे का बार-बार रोना हो सकता है — रोने के आम कारणों में कब्ज़ भी शामिल है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [2]। रोने के और भी कारण हो सकते हैं: भूख, गीला या गंदा नैपी, गैस, थकान, गोद में आने की इच्छा, ज़्यादा गर्मी या ठंड, बोरियत या ज़्यादा उत्तेजना [3]।

अभी के लिए: बच्चे को गोद में लेकर आराम पहुँचाने की कोशिश करें और रोना शांत होने का इंतज़ार करें [1]। अगर पता न चले कि क्या परेशानी है, तो अपने डॉक्टर से बात करें [2]।

मदद कब लें — अगर बच्चा:
- लगातार रो रहा हो और शांत न हो पाए, या रोना आम रोने जैसा न लगे [4]
- तेज़ बुखार हो या दूध/खाना लेने में दिलचस्पी न हो [4]
- रोने के बीच फिर सामान्य न हो पाए [6]
- पीलापन, पसीना, सुस्ती या दूध लेने से इनकार करे [6]
- बुखार, उल्टी या खून वाली पॉटी हो [6]

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार के दौरान हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना आम बात है: जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे को ठंड लगती है, कभी-कभी कंपकंपी भी होती है, और खासकर हाथों-पैरों की त्वचा पर जाल जैसा रंग दिख सकता है, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [2]। बुखार खुद बीमारी नहीं, बल्कि शरीर के बचाव का संकेत है, और आमतौर पर इसका कारण कोई साधारण, अक्सर वायरल, संक्रमण होता है [4]।

अभी बच्चे को पर्याप्त तरल पदार्थ पिलाएँ, ताकि निर्जलीकरण न हो [1]। बुखार से परेशानी हो तो डॉक्टर पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन जैसी दवा की सलाह दे सकते हैं; बच्चों को एस्पिरिन नहीं देनी चाहिए [1]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न पर निर्भर करती है — PediBot के डोज़ कैलकुलेटर से पता कर सकते हैं।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- बुखार बहुत तेज़ हो या बना रहे [1]
- बच्चा सुस्त, बेहोश या भ्रमित लगे [6]
- उल्टी हो या तेज़ सिरदर्द [6]
- तेज़ प्यास, कम पेशाब या सूखे होंठ (निर्जलीकरण) [1]

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
बच्चे का सुस्त होना और ठीक से जाग न पाना गंभीरता का संकेत है, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार निमोनिया में यह खतरे का लक्षण माना जाता है [2]। ऐसे में तुरंत वैद्यकीय सहायता लेना चाहिए [2]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को अपने पास रखें और उसका ध्यान रखें। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार बच्चे का खान-पान चालू रखने की कोशिश करें [2]। अगर बुखार हो तो गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं [2]।

विकासपीडिया के अनुसार निमोनिया में ये खतरे के लक्षण हैं [2]:
- बुखार से दौरे पड़ना [2]
- खाने-पीने या स्तनपान से मना करना [2]
- साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचना [2]
- सीने से कराहने या सीटी जैसी आवाज़ आना [2]
- त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून या चेहरे पर नीली झलक [2]
sources: [2] Vikaspedia — "बच्चों को होने वाली आम बीमारियॉं — स्रोत: भारत स्वास्थ्य" (2020), sectio

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
बच्चे का पेशाब कम आना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और ऐसे में तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलना ज़रूरी है [1]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन पिलाते रहें [1]। बच्चे को भूखा न रखें — सामान्य खाना जारी रखें, बस थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार, बच्चे की भूख का ध्यान रखते हुए [1]। ज़्यादा चिकनाई वाले खाने, मिठाइयों और जूस से बचें [1]। दूध और स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से जारी रखें, और अगर बच्चा मांगे तो और भी बार-बार कराएं [1]। स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक न दें, क्योंकि उनमें चीनी बहुत ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट का स्तर बच्चे के लिए अनुपयुक्त होता है [1]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी करे, ठोस या तरल कुछ भी न रख पाए, या बिना कुछ पिए भी उल्टी करे, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर के पास जाना ज़रूरी है।

बड़े बच्चे में बुखार शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की सामान्य प्रतिक्रिया है, और तापमान आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में सामान्य हो जाता है [3]। त्वचा पर बैंगनी या ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर नहीं मिटते, तेज़ बुखार के साथ, गंभीर संक्रमण का संकेत हैं [1][2]।

अभी क्या करें: बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें, और उसे ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े न उतारें या स्पंज न करें [2]। बुखार नापने के लिए डिजिटल थर्मामीटर बगल में रखें [3]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर है, इसलिए डॉक्टर जो बताएँ वही दें। 16 साल से छोटे बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें, और डॉक्टर के कहे बिना आइबुप्रोफेन और पैरासिटामोल बारी-बारी न दें [2]।

मदद कब लें — इनमें से कोई भी लक्षण दिखे तो तुरंत:
- बच्चा सुस्त, कम प्रतिक्रिया देने वाला या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा [1]
- साँस लेने में तकलीफ [1]
- कुछ भी खाना-पीना न ले पाना [1]
- गर्दन में अकड़न, रोशनी से परेशानी, दौरा [2]
- हाथ-पैर असामान्य रूप से ठंडे, त्वचा का रंग नीला, धूसर या पीला पड़ना [2]

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text:
Paracetamol bukhar aur takleef mein madad karta hai, aur ise har 4-6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai — din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi, AEPap ke mutabiq [3]. Aapke 3 saal ke bacche ke liye sahi matra (dose) uske wazan par nirnay hoti hai, umar par nahi [3]. PediBot ka dose calculator paracetamol ke liye maujood hai, jahan wazan daal kar sahi matra nikli ja sakti hai.

Dawa dene se pehle bacche ki haalat dekhein. Agar koi khatre ka ishara nahi hai, to pehle sharirik tarike aazmayein: zyada kapde utarein, tara l dein, activity kam karein, aur agar bacche ko theek lage to halke garam paani se nahane dein [6]. Agar bukhar se takleef ho rahi hai to antitemik dein [3].

Ibuprofen 3 saal ke bacche ko diya ja sakta hai (6 mahine se bade bachon mein mana nahi), lekin AEPap kehti hai ki shuruaat paracetamol se karein aur ibuprofen ko vikalp ke roop mein rakhein [3]. Ibuprofen har 6-8 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai [3].

Madad lein agar:
- Bukhar 38-38.5°C se upar ho aur takleef ho [3]
- 3-4 ghante baad bhi bukhar aur takleef kam na ho [3]
- Lagatar ulti ho (ibuprofen na dein) [3]
- Bacche ko doray (convulsion) pad chuke hon [3]

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi hona aam taur par sardi-zukaam ya asthma jaisi saans ki takleef ka hissa ho sakta hai. MedlinePlus ke mutabiq bachchon mein asthma ki khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [1].

Ghar par: khansi ke liye koi ilaaj nahi hai, lekin aaram, khoob saara tarral (liquid), saaf humidifier ya thanda vaporizer, aur saline naak ki boondein madad karti hain [6]. Sardi-zukaam mein khansi 10 se 14 din tak reh sakti hai [4]. SEUP ke mutabiq khansi ke syrup, mucolytics ya corticoides faydemand nahi hain [2].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Saans lene mein sakht dikkat ya tez saans [1]
- Honth, chehra ya naakhun neele pad jaayein [1][3]
- Seene mein kasav ya seeti ki awaaz [1][3]
- Doodh peena ya khana mushkil ho [1]
- Bukhaar jo 4 din se zyada rahe [6]

Agar bachcha 3 mahine se chhota hai ya use pehle se koi saans ki bimari hai, to zyada dhyan dein [5].

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Red, itchy spots on the feet can be heat rash (prickly heat), which is uncomfortable but usually harmless and gets better on its own in a few days, according to the NHS [6]. It can appear anywhere on the body and spread, but it cannot be passed on to other people [6].

To help now: keep the skin cool so it does not sweat and irritate the rash — loose cotton clothing, lightweight bedding, cool baths or showers, and plenty of fluids [6]. To calm the itching, apply something cold such as a damp cloth or an ice pack wrapped in a tea towel for up to 20 minutes, and tap or pat the rash instead of scratching it [6]. Do not use perfumed shower gels or creams [6].

Get help if:
- swelling around the mouth [5]
- struggling to breathe [5]

q: mera bachcha bed se gir gaya aur ek baar ulti ki
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
Bed se girne ke baad ek baar ulti hona — SEUP ke mutabik, sirf is ek lakshan se ye tay nahi hota ki kitni chot lagi hai; zaroori ye hai ki bachche ko turant doctor dikhaya jaye, kyunki sir ki chot ke baad ulti aana ek aisa lakshan hai jiske liye turant jaanch zaroori hai [1].

Jab tak aap doctor ke paas pahunch rahe hain: bachche ko aaram se, sar thoda uncha karke rakhein, aur use akela na chhodein [1]. Kuch khilane-peelane ke liye zabardasti na karein; agar bachcha peena chahe to thode-thode ghoont paani de sakte hain [3].

SEUP ke mutabik, in baaton par turant dhyan dein aur doctor ko batayein [1][3]:
- 3 mahine se chhota bachcha [1]
- 1 metre se zyada unchi jagah se girna [1]
- baar-baar ulti, ya kuch bhi andar na rukna [3]
- ulti hari, khoon wali, ya coffee-jaisi [3]
- neend mein, sust, bahut pyaas, dhundhe aankh, aansu ke bina rona, kam peshab [3]
- tez sar dard ya pet dard [3]

Agar bachcha behosh ho, saans theek na le, ya uthne par jawab na de, to turant madad lein [1].

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Kuchh babies ka rona zyada hota hai, aur kabhi kabhi iska matlab kabz bhi ho sakta hai — NHS ke mutabiq rone ki aam wajahon mein kabz bhi shamil hai [3]. Agar bachcha potty karte waqt rota hai, to yeh takleef ki nishani ho sakti hai.

Abhi ke liye: bachche ko aaram se pakad kar tasalli dein, aur pet ko halke haath se sehlayein. Agar doodh pila rahi hain to position aur attachment theek karne se madad mil sakti hai [5]. Kabz ke liye koi dawa khud na dein — apne doctor se poochhein.

Doctor se milein agar:
- rona lagatar hai aur tasalli se band nahi hota [7]
- rona aam rone jaisa nahi lagta [7]
- bachcha doodh lena band kar de ya kam kar de [7]
- bukhar ho [7]
- 8 ghante se peshab (wet nappy) na hua ho [7]

Agar bachche ko daure (fit) aayein, saans lene mein dikkat ho, ya skin neeli, grey ya pale ho jaye, to turant emergency help lein [7].

q: mere bete ko saans lene mein dikkat lag rahi hai
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: साँस लेने में गंभीर दिक्कत (पसलियाँ दिखना, बहुत तेज़ साँस, साँस रुकना, नीलापन)
text:
Saans lene mein dikkat kai cheezon se ho sakti hai, jaise bronchiolitis ya RSV, jo shuruaat mein zukam jaisa lagta hai aur kuch dinon mein badh sakta hai [5][2]. Aap jo lakshan bata rahe hain — saans lene mein dikkat — in sources mein ek aise lakshan ke roop mein diya gaya hai jiske liye turant madad leni chahiye [5].

Jab tak madad aa rahi hai: bachche ko seedha rakhein aur shaant rakhein, aur unhe kuch khilane-pilane ke liye majboor na karein agar woh nahi le raha [5]. Agar bachcha doodh ya khaana kam le raha hai, to thoda-thoda baar-baar dena behtar hai [5].

Yeh cheezein zyada gambhir hone ka sanket hain:
- Saans lene mein dikkat, pet andar khinch raha ho ya grunting ho [5]
- Saans lene mein rukawat ya pause [5]
- Hont, jeebh ya skin neeli ya grey ho jaye [5]
- Bachcha bahut sust ho aur jagane par na jage [5]
- Khaana-peena bahut kam ho jaye ya dehydration ke lakshan [5]

q: meri beti bahut sust hai aur jag nahi rahi
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
Meri beti ki susti aur jag na paana gambhir lakshan ho sakte hain. WHO ke mutabik sepsis ek medical emergency hai, aur bachchon mein iske lakshan hain tez saans, jhatke, phiki twacha, susti aur jagane mein mushkil [4]. SEUP bhi kehta hai ki atyadhik neend ya bachche ko jagane mein problem hona ek cheez hai jiske liye turant urgent care lena chahiye [7].

Jab tak madad mil rahi hai: agar bachcha behosh hai aur saans nahi le raha to CPR shuru karein; agar behosh hai lekin saans le raha hai to recovery position mein rakhein; saans check karte rahein aur baat karte rahein taaki hosh na khoye [6]. Unhe kuch khilayein ya pilayein nahi [6].

Agar bachche ko jhatke aa rahe hain, honth ya twacha neeli, grey ya phiki ho rahi hai, saans lene mein dikkat ho rahi hai, ya wo behosh ya bahut floppy ho raha hai, to turant ambulance bulayein [3].

q: mera bachcha bahut tez saans le raha hai
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
तेज़ साँस लेना ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस या निमोनिया जैसी स्थितियों में हो सकता है — NHS के अनुसार ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस में शुरुआत ज़ुकाम जैसी होती है, फिर खाँसी और तेज़ साँस चलना शुरू होता है [3]। WHO के अनुसार 5 साल से छोटे बच्चों में खाँसी या साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ के साथ तेज़ साँस चलना निमोनिया का संकेत हो सकता है [6]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को सीधा बैठाएँ या गोद में सहारा देकर रखें, और थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार तरल दें — NHS कहता है कि ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस में बच्चा कम खाता-पीता है, इसलिए तरल बनाए रखना ज़रूरी है [3]। बच्चे को अकेला न छोड़ें और उसकी साँस पर नज़र रखें [3]।

इलाज के लिए जाते समय ये संकेत बताएँ: साँस लेते वक्त पसलियाँ अंदर धँसना या पेट का नीचे का हिस्सा दबना [3][6], साँस में रुकावट या ठहराव [3], होंठ, जीभ या चेहरा नीला या स्लेटी पड़ना [3], बहुत सुस्त होना या जागते न रहना [3], दूध या खाना बिल्कुल न लेना [3][6]।

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A bad night-time cough in a 2-year-old is often worse at night, and in whooping cough the coughing bouts are worse at night and can last for several weeks [2][3]. Croup also causes a barking cough that is often worse at night [5].

Keep the room calm and let your child rest; small sips of fluid help if they are coughing a lot. Do not give honey if your child is under 12 months — at 24 months it is not a concern, but the sources here do not cover honey.

Get help if:
- The cough is very bad and getting worse [4]
- Lips, tongue, face or skin turn blue or grey [4]
- Hard or shallow breathing [4]
- Chest pain worse when breathing or coughing [4]
- Seizures (fits) [4]

If you think it may be croup, ask your doctor — medicine may shorten the illness [5].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text:
A rash that spreads over the whole body can be caused by more than one illness, and the pattern matters. In measles, the rash usually starts on the face and upper neck and moves down over about three days to the chest, arms, legs and feet, and it usually fades on its own in four to eight days, according to the WHO [4]. Before the rash, there are usually four to seven days of fever, runny nose, cough and red, watery eyes, and small white spots inside the cheeks [4].

Chickenpox is another cause: an itchy rash that turns into fluid-filled blisters and then scabs, often starting on the face, chest and back before spreading, and it usually lasts five to ten days, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Calamine lotion and oatmeal baths can help the itch, and acetaminophen can help with fever — but do not give aspirin, because with chickenpox it can cause Reye syndrome [5].

Get help if:
- Trouble breathing or severe breathing problems [4]
- Confusion, drowsiness or a seizure [4]
- Severe diarrhoea or signs of dehydration [4]
- An ear infection [4]
- The child is under five or malnourished, which raises the risk of complications [4]

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text:
It is common for children to refuse food for a while, and worrying about it is natural, according to the NHS [5]. What matters more is what they eat over a week rather than in a single day [5].

Keep offering a variety of foods from the four main food groups — fruit and vegetables; potatoes, bread, rice, pasta and other starchy carbohydrates; dairy or dairy alternatives; and beans, pulses, fish, eggs, meat and other proteins [5]. Give small portions, praise them for eating even a little, and try a rejected food again another time — tastes change [2][5]. Do not force them to eat [2].

Get help if:
- Refusing to eat or drink [1]
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [1]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [1]
- Persistent or intense tummy pain, or stools with a lot of blood [1]
- Vomiting a lot, not keeping down solids or liquids, or vomit that is green, bloody or like coffee grounds [3]

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A whistling or wheezing sound with a congested chest in a 6-month-old is often bronchiolitis, which usually starts like a cold and can cause noisy breathing and difficulty feeding, according to the NHS [2]. Symptoms are usually worst between days 3 and 5, and the cough usually gets better in 3 weeks [2].

Keep feeding them little and often, and watch their breathing and how much they are drinking [2].

Get help now if:
- They are feeding much less than normal [2]
- A dry nappy for 12 hours or more, or other signs of dehydration [2]
- They seem very tired, irritable or not themselves [2]
- Their breathing gets harder — ribs pulling in, tummy sucking under the ribs, or grunting [2][5]
- Their skin, tongue or lips look blue or grey [2]

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार छोटे बच्चों में बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिन में उतर जाता है, एनएचएस के अनुसार [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — स्तनपान कराने वाली माँ सामान्य रूप से स्तनपान जारी रखें [3]। निर्जलीकरण के संकेतों पर नज़र रखें [3]। बच्चा खाना चाहे तो दें [3]। रात में भी नियमित रूप से बच्चे को देखते रहें [3]। बच्चे को घर पर रखें [3]। अगर बच्चा परेशान या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दें — पैकेजिंग या पत्ते पर देखें कि दवा आपके बच्चे के लिए उपयुक्त है या नहीं, या फार्मासिस्ट या डॉक्टर से पूछें [3]। 6 महीने और 5 किलो वज़न वाले बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें, क्योंकि 3 महीने से छोटे या 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले बच्चों को आइबुप्रोफेन नहीं देना चाहिए [2]। खुराक बच्चे के वज़न पर निर्भर करती है।

मदद कब लें:
- 3 से 6 महीने के बच्चे का तापमान 39°C या ज़्यादा [2]
- बुखार के साथ दाने जैसे बीमारी के अन्य संकेत [2]
- बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [2]
- खाना न चाहे या सामान्य न लगे और आप चिंतित हों [2]
- निर्जलीकरण — कम गीले नैपी, धँसी आँखें, रोते समय आँसू न आना [2]

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार में बच्चे को नहलाना या स्पंज करके ठंडा करने की कोशिश न करें — यह शरीर की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]। बुखार आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में अपने आप सामान्य हो जाता है [1]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं, और बच्चे का खाना-पीना चालू रखें, ऐसा भारत स्वास्थ्य कहता है [3]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [7]। पैरासिटामोल से बुखार का इलाज किया जा सकता है [6] — खुराक बच्चे के वज़न के हिसाब से तय होती है।

तुरंत मदद लें अगर:
- 3 से 6 महीने का बच्चा और तापमान 39°C या ज़्यादा [7]
- बुखार के साथ दाने [7]
- बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [7]
- खाने से मना करे या हमेशा जैसा न लगे [7]
- पेशाब कम आना, धँसी आँखें, रोते समय आँसू न आना [7]

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
3 साल के बच्चे में सूखी खांसी और सांस लेते समय सीटी जैसी आवाज़ होना, SEUP के अनुसार, ब्रोंकियल ट्यूब में रुकावट के कारण होने वाली श्वास की समस्या का संकेत है [2]। यह अक्सर सर्दी-जुकाम या वायरल संक्रमण से शुरू होती है, और प्रीस्कूल उम्र के बच्चों में सीटी की आवाज़ का सबसे आम कारण श्वसन संक्रमण ही होता है [2]।

अभी क्या करें: बच्चे को शांत रखें और सीधा बैठाएं, ताकि सांस लेना आसान हो। SEUP के अनुसार, ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर दवाएं (जैसे सल्ब्यूटामोल) सांस की नली की रुकावट को कम करती हैं [2] — लेकिन दवा और उसकी मात्रा के बारे में अपने डॉक्टर से पूछें, क्योंकि यह बच्चे के वजन पर निर्भर करती है।

NHS के अनुसार, अगर बच्चे को क्रूप हो सकता है तो डॉक्टर से तुरंत मिलें, क्योंकि दवा बीमारी को छोटा कर सकती है [3]। MedlinePlus के अनुसार, तेज़ खांसी, सांस लेने में गंभीर तकलीफ़, या चेहरे, होंठ और नाखूनों का पीला या नीला पड़ना गंभीर दौरे के चेतावनी संकेत हैं — ऐसे में तुरंत मदद लें [7]।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल दाने और खुजली कई कारणों से हो सकते हैं। बहुत खुजली वाले उभरे हुए दाने छोटे कीड़ों (स्केबीज़) से हो सकते हैं, जो त्वचा में घुसकर अंडे देते हैं; उंगलियों के बीच एक सिरे पर बिंदु वाली उभरी लकीरें दिख सकती हैं, और स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही हो जाता है [4]। स्केबीज़ में तेज़ खुजली और दाने होते हैं और यह त्वचा के सीधे संपर्क से फैलता है [2]।

घर पर: ठंडे पानी से नहाएँ और त्वचा को थपथपाकर सुखाएँ, रगड़ें नहीं; ढीले कपड़े पहनाएँ; खुजली के लिए फार्मासिस्ट से एंटीहिस्टामिन के बारे में पूछें [5]। नाखून छोटे काटें और रात में हाथों में मोज़े पहनाएँ ताकि बच्चा खुजाए नहीं [5]। खुजली शुरू होने के बाद कुछ हफ़्तों तक बनी रह सकती है [1]।

मदद लें अगर:
- त्वचा में संक्रमण लगने का संदेह हो [1]
- एक्ज़िमा जैसी कोई और त्वचा समस्या हो [1]
- कोहनी, घुटनों, हाथों या पैरों पर पपड़ीदार परतदार दाने हों [1]
- फार्मेसी का इलाज पूरा होने के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे [1]

स्केबीज़ का इलाज क्रीम या मुँह से ली जाने वाली दवाओं से होता है [2]।

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है — सभी टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं, और होने वाले दुष्प्रभाव मामूली से गंभीर तक हो सकते हैं पर इनका मामूली उपचार से इलाज हो जाता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना यह संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर दिखा रही है [6]।

भारत में टीकाकरण की उम्र और खुराक राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती हैं — अपने बच्चे के टीके कब लगेंगे, यह अपने डॉक्टर या स्वास्थ्य कार्यकर्ता से पूछ लें [4]। टीके समय पर लगवाना सबसे अच्छी सुरक्षा के लिए ज़रूरी है, और अगर कोई टीका छूट गया हो तो डॉक्टर से मिलकर उसे पूरा करवाया जा सकता है [4]।

टीके सुरक्षित और प्रभावी हैं और जान बचा सकते हैं [4]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi 3 saal ke bachche mein aam hai, aur aksar yeh sardi-zukam ya asthma jaisi sthiti se juda hota hai. MedlinePlus ke mutabik bachchon mein asthma ke lakshan hain: seene mein jakadan, khaas taur par raat ya subah jaldi khansi, saans lene mein dikkat, thakan, aankhon ke neeche kaale ghere, chidchidapan aur saans chhodte waqt seeti jaisi awaaz [5].

Ghar par: bachche ko aaram karne dein, khoob saari taral cheezein (paani, soup) pilayein, kamre mein saaf humidifier ya thanda vaporizer rakhein, aur saline nasal drops ya spray istemal karein [4]. Khansi ya dard ke liye koi bhi dawa dene se pehle apne bachche ke doctor ya pharmacist se poochein, kyunki kuch khansi-sardi ki dawaiyon mein aise ingredients hote hain jo bachchon ke liye nahi recommend kiye jaate [4]. Bachchon ko aspirin bilkul na dein [4].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Saans lene mein dikkat ya tez saans [4]
- Hothon ya chehre par neela ya peela rang [5]
- Bahut sust ya behosh jaisa [7]
- Khansi ke saath seene ka gehna dhadakna ya pasliyan dikhna [7]
- Bukhar 4 din se zyada [4]
